utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. For the record, all the accused are here. Defence teams, I notice the absence of Mr. Haynes, Mr. Josse. But I am seeing a new face in the Gvero team.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. May I introduce a new member of our team. This is Ivan Zogovic, our new legal consultant. It doesn't mean that Mr. Josse is leaving.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZOGOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Ivan Zogovic and I am honoured to be part of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have your name again? Because I want it for the record because the interpreters missed it. UNKNOWN PERSON: Ivan Zogovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ivan Zogovic. Thank you, Mr. Zogovic. You're most welcome. And we'll have the opportunity to see you working in the Gvero Defence team. For the Prosecution, I only notice the presence of Mr. McCloskey today. The witness is here. Remind me after the break, because I needed to say something about Pandurevic and Borovcanin motion on protective measures but I wouldn't like to deal with it in the circumstances as they are now. So in the break, we'll deal with that before the new witness actually is ushered in, okay? Thank you. Or we can deal with it actually when this witness finishes and before the next one starts. Yes, good morning to you, Mr. Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey will continue his cross-examination. Go ahead, Mr. McCloskey and good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were you able to think of or remember the names of the people or person that helped obtain Hotel Fontana documents for you?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Brane Ilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And what was Brane Ilic's position at the time, do you know, during the -- 1995?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he had the authorities like any other employee. His position was that of a head in the absence of the director and before the receivership was started and before the receiver was appointed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know who the director of the Hotel Fontana was in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who was that, name?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I met him just once, and see, since at the time he was no longer director, I did not make much effort to retain his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. When our investigators went there a while back, they met with a person named Nedjeljko Ilic. Does that ring any bells?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How about Milena Tomic?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nedjeljko does not ring any bells and Mrs. Tomic does.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is your memory related to Ms. Tomic and this issue of the Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The hotel is a very complex organisation with a number of business units, not only in the territory of the municipality but even in other places, and this particular lady worked for an accountant. She was very helpful and she assisted us when it came to looking for these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did she provide you with documents? Was she actually one of the people that provided you with the documents that you mentioned earlier?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ilic was the one who personally gave the documents to me, but everybody else participated in the search for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So Mr. Ilic and anybody else besides Ms. Tomic and Ilic? When you say "everybody," that sounds like a group.

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said it. The accountant, the treasurer, and the person who coordinated the whole thing in a way, from the moment when we entered to the moment when all the documents were photocopied and whatever technical stuff had to be done with the documents. As far as the procedure went and everything else, I did not need to get in touch with everybody. The procedure was very fair, very professional, and given the situation of the archives, I believe that they did it correctly and in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you had mentioned that you had met with many witnesses for your team and made an effort to get close to them, which is normal. Did that include the next witness, Dragan Stojkic?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just like I did with one, I did with all, all of them, over 300 witnesses. Given the frustration that still existed after so many years, in people, in general, all these contacts were always identical, almost without any differences, and the same went to the next witness, Mr. Stojkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you also meet with Zoran Acimovic, the witness after that?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. You're asking me how we met. What do you mean when you say that? The first time? Now? When?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I didn't -- maybe there was a translation issue. It was a much simpler question than that. It was just did you meet, in your investigation, Zoran Acimovic?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw Zoran. First I had to establish the identity of the person, to see whether that was that person, not only by name, and so on and so forth, and I did that with everybody, so I had a personal first contact with Zoran Acimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And in the information that was provided by the Defence to us, there is a brief reference to a communications logbook that the communications guys had at the IKM. Are you aware of that logbook?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that that book existed, the logbook from the IKM.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you ever see it or see a copy of it?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no need for me to ask for it personally and to start any proceedings that were necessary based on that particular logbook. To put it simply, even without that logbook, I had ample elements to meet with these persons who had been at the IKM.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just so I'm perfectly clear, I'm not talking about the duty officer IKM logbook. I am talking about a logbook that the communications guys say they had, separate from the duty officer book. Is that what you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even if there had been such a logbook, this is the first time I hear of its existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you didn't ask anyone for the communications logbook of the communications officers?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have such a question because I did not have any foundations for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, you may have noticed in your investigation that when we searched the Zvornik Brigade we didn't get daily combat reports from the battalions or very many actual battalion records from the Zvornik Brigade battalions. In your investigation, did you find any records from the Zvornik Brigade battalions?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my work, I did not come across any such records. Nor did I touch upon that issue of a possible existence of this type of documentation during my conversations and interviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You mentioned, in your direct testimony, that you obtained materials from Serbia. Can you give us a brief outline of the kinds of materials you obtained from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the MUP of Serbia, we were supposed to get in touch with their organisational units, in particular regions, where we were supposed to establish whether certain persons were staying there, based on the information that were available to us, in order to establish personal contacts with them, which means that we were supposed to establish the place of residence of those people who had once resided in the territory of Podrinje municipalities and as far as --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, again, it's a simple question. Can you just outline what the sorts of materials you obtained from Serbia, if any? And you can always explain it, but it works better if you answer the question first and then explain.

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Materials were obtained in the sense of the documentation about persons, and as for any other documentation, we did not search or made application to obtain any other documentation from any other organs of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So what sort of documentation about what sort of persons? Are we talking Serb persons or Muslim persons?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were Serbs who first resided and then for various reasons they moved to live and took the citizenship of Serbia or they found employment and moved out with their families to the territory of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And before starting to work for the Popovic team, did you know any of the accused in this case personally?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew a few of them personally, a few of the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, can you just tell us who you knew and how well you knew them?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to the same grammar school in Sokolac, which, in the past, in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, was reputed as the -- one of the best schools in the republic, according to the criteria --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- this is again another very simple question. Can you tell us -- and I don't want to go into a whole lot of detail about this. I just want to know by name which accused you knew personally. Let's just start with why don't you give us a list of the names of the guys you knew before you worked on the case?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew Mr. Vinko Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Who else?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also met, on several occasions, Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I also met Mr. Gvero during the war. And that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you work with Mr. Borovcanin in the MUP during the war?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't work with him. We did work in the same ministry, however, because I belonged to the -- as it was called at the time -- the Sarajevo-Birac centre headquartered in Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how well did you know Vinko Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it would be irrelevant to speak about the extent of that friendship, to put it that way, because our families, our two families, had multiple ties in the area. We are related. We were each other's best men and godfathers. The ties are various and multiple.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And did you know Vinko Pandurevic when he was stationed in Visegrad in 1992?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Madam Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, good morning to everybody in the courtroom. I have just one question in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, my learned friend asked you about Brane Ilic. Did you only meet him after the war?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, after the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, the Bench doesn't have any questions for you, which means that your testimony finishes here. On behalf of the Trial Chamber, I wish to thank you for having come over to give testimony, and on behalf of everyone I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's deal with the exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we had expected our list to have arrived, which was prepared for disclosure. Anyway -- ah, it's just arrived. We apologies for the slight delay but it's here. So we tender the following exhibits, that is to say the exhibits on our list be tendered into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, we just got the six pages of the list. And we don't have any objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It was -- I understand that it was available also before, no?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There was something available but we would just, as the custom is, to mark the many untranslated documents and wait until they get translated for the final decision. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Any objections from any of the other Defence teams? None. So they are also so admitted with the caveat that Mr. McCloskey has just referred to, those which are still untranslated will, for the time being, be marked for identification. Thank you. There are some Prosecution exhibits as well. No?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. Though I would request the Court request the Popovic team to turn over the documents from the Hotel Fontana that were the subject of direct testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I've asked the team informally and didn't really get a response. I think they told me no. But I asked them on Friday and I asked them again this morning. This, as the Court is aware, part of this area of the law is a little muddy in the Tribunal and I don't wish to get into that at this point but I think what makes this particular situation stand out above the law regarding materials in the possession of the Defence is that they brought this up in direct testimony where the person described the kinds of logs and documents that were obtained by the Hotel Fontana. This isn't me probing into the Defence or finding out about the Defence, and they mention that to you and I think that we are now entitled to, at the very minimum, see those documents to determine if there is any relevance to them. That's why I would ask that we be allowed to see those. And we can provide written submissions on this issue, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The Popovic Defence on two occasions just prior to the Defence case did disclose to the Prosecutor pursuant to Rule 67(A) documents, because we considered it our duty to disclose to the Prosecution what we were going to use during our Defence case. The documents which the witness mentioned during his testimony are not on our 65 ter list and we have no intention of using them. And so we -- none of these documents were presented, so we don't see any reason to comply with the rule in this particular instance.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do apologise but the interpretation wasn't correct, the last sentence. What I said was that the Popovic Defence does not see anything in the Rules of Procedure and Evidence to have additional disclosure because the documents were not used and presented to the witness and are not on the list so we see no reason for any additional disclosure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. McCloskey, thank you, Ms. Tapuskovic. Things being what they seem to be, if you want to pursue the matter, you will need to file a proper motion and then we will give the opportunity to the Popovic Defence team to reply, and decide it accordingly. So before we bring in the next witness, the -- some time back, on the 21st of May actually, the Vinko Pandurevic Defence team filed a motion for protective measures in regard to two witnesses, namely Witness 7DW-14 and 7DW-12, who is also happens also to be witness 4DW-16. Two days later, the Borovcanin Defence team through a filing joined the Pandurevic motion insofar as it relates to the witness that is on both lists, specifically the Borovcanin team, although joining the Pandurevic Defence team, makes a submission which is different from that contained in the Pandurevic motion. Let me explain why. The Pandurevic motion, in their motion -- the Pandurevic motion in relation to Witness 7DW-14, apart from the usual pseudonym, seeks also the deferred disclosure of this witness's identity until 30 days before he testifies. In relation to Witness 7DW-12, who was also Witness 4DW-16 there is the same request. The Borovcanin team, in relation to this last witness, seeks the delayed disclosure until 30 days before the anticipated start of the Borovcanin Defence case. This, as you see, is somewhat different from what is contained in the Pandurevic motion. We need first to establish whether there is agreement between the Borovcanin Defence team and the Pandurevic Defence team that their common witness, namely 7DW-12, who is also 4DW-16, will testify in the Borovcanin Defence case, and the purpose of asking this question is to ensure that the Pandurevic Defence team agrees that in that case, they will conduct the examination-in-chief during this gentleman's testimony in the Borovcanin Defence. Do we have -- Mr. Sarapa, do you confirm that this is what will happen?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, do I expect that to be the case. However, if you give us some time, during the break, I'll be able to tell you when I'll meet my colleagues from the Borovcanin team and then we will be able to come up with a definitive answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. The next -- thank you. You need to make it clear that since the Borovcanin Defence case will start before yours and this guy is a witness on the Borovcanin Defence list, he is going to testify during that Defence case, but we are expecting that you conduct your examination-in-chief when he -- when the Borovcanin Defence case is being dealt with. All right? The other thing is this: This raises the question as to when the disclosure should take place, whether it should be delayed until 30 days before he testifies or 30 days before the commencement of the Borovcanin Defence case. And I'm raising this because my understanding is, Mr. McCloskey, that you don't really object to either. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But we can't leave it hanging like that, so in other words, we need to know whether you are prepared to take a common position, the Borovcanin and the Pandurevic Defence team, or whether you wish to retain your separate position on this, in which case we will of course decide according to what we will consider in the best interests of justice.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At all events, we won't need a ruling from the Trial Chamber. We will reach an agreement during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I'm almost certain that the witness will come in just once and testify as a witness for us all but I'll let you know after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I'm talking now about the disclosure, whether it should be delayed one way or whether it should be delayed the other way. That also, you need to discuss amongst yourselves. Let us know because we need to discuss it. Later on during the second break we will hand down an oral decision on this, after having heard the outcome of your consultations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We will hold our consultations during the first break and we will inform you of the results immediately afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. So this is postponed until later. Are we ready to start with the next witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And welcome to this Tribunal. You're about to start giving evidence, as a witness produced, brought forward, by the Defence team of Colonel Vujadin Popovic. Before you give evidence, you're required by our rules to make a solemn declaration equivalent to an oath that in the course of your testimony, you will be speaking the truth. Madam Usher is going to hand you the text. Please read it out aloud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, sir. Please make yourself comfortable. You will now be asked a series of questions by Mr. Zivanovic, who will introduce himself to you and then we'll see who else wishes to put questions to you. Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stojkic, we've already met but let me repeat, I'm Zoran Zivanovic and in these proceedings I'm Defence counsel for Vujadin Popovic. First of all for the record, could you give us your first and last name, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Dragan Stojkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And tell me, please, your place and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: On the 11th of October 1960, Celopek.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]. What schooling have you had?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Primary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us briefly where you worked until now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: In the footwear factory, Standard.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that in Zvornik or in some other place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Karakaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you do your military service?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And where was that, what branch of the services?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Signalsman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And where were you living in 1991?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Celopek.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that also Zvornik municipality?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you mobilised at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And where were you mobilised, to which unit, which branch of the army, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: In Bijeljina, the infantry first.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what year that was?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was that the JNA, the former army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And how long did you serve in that JNA unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: I was there twice, with one interruption.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What was the interruption?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: I had a disagreement with the major, Major Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: And later on I returned in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you wounded ever?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: On the 19th of May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you join the army of Republika Srpska at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was that a consequence or were you wounded within that situation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And which unit were you deployed in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Celopek, the company belonging to the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The answer was yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we need an answer from the witness on line 19, or rather page 19 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me repeat the question. I'll repeat the question. I see there are no answers to two questions. The second one is more important, as far as I'm concerned. My question was this: When did that happen? When were you wounded?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: The 19th of May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you failed to answer another question. In the army of Republika Srpska, did you become a member once you had recovered from your injuries?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, what branch of the services were you in the brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: I was in the infantry first and then I became a signalsman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And when did you become a signalsman? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you stay a signalsman until the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes, and even after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please, in this signals unit of the Zvornik Brigade, what jobs did you perform, what work?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: I worked in the brigade on the IKM, the forward command post, and the switchboard.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And where was the switchboard?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: You mean in the barracks?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: It was on the third floor, as you go up the stairs, it's the last office to the left, or, rather, to the right, looking onto the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the IKM. Could you tell me where that forward command post was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes, in Kitovnice.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And how far is that from Zvornik, roughly speaking?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Perhaps some 20 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you now tell me, please, when you did your work, while you were working on the switchboard, and perhaps at the IKM at Kitovnice, what equipment did you have in your work?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: At the IKM, TC 10 and the RUP 12 device. And in the brigade, MG 100 and the in-house switchboard.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you just tell us briefly, very briefly, what is this TC 10 device?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: It's a telephone switchboard, a military one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How about the RUP 12?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: It's the radio relay device.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever work with radio relay devices of RRU-1 or RRU-800?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What about a teleprinter?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, when you were working at the forward command post, how long would you stay there in a stretch? What was your duty there? How long did your shift last at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Four days.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And what were your duties, you as a signalsman? What were your duties at this forward command post? What did your job entail?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Well, someone manning the TC 10, RUP 12, receiving information from the battalion, I conveyed the information to the duty officer at the IKM, the officer on duty at the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in addition to you as the signalsman, who else manned the IKM? Who else was there while you were working? Was there anybody else who had the duty of being there with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: You mean together with us two? There were two of us. And then there was the duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that it was your duty, and I assume the duty of this other signalsman, was to work four-day shifts, four-day shifts up at the IKM. Now, can you tell me what the duration of -- how long the shift lasted for the duty officers? How long were their shifts?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And when did they start, when did one shift take over from another?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: It was from 8.00 to 8.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the forward command post, were any records kept, any logbooks, any notebooks, anything of that kind by you and the officers on duty or officer on duty?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether you, as signalsman, had a notebook of any kind or a book in which you recorded anything, made entries, and, if so, tell me straight away what you had, what kind of book you had and what entries you made.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Every report from the battalion would be recorded in our book as signalsman and handed -- and then we would hand it over to the officer on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And was there a book, a notebook, some record, where the officer on duty wrote in entries?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: As signalsman, did you have the right to make any entries into the book kept by the officer on duty?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Another question: What was the forward command post? Was it located in a house or in some other premises? What was the IKM, in fact? Where was it situated?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I'll rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please describe the house which housed the IKM?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't think he's doing it on purpose but in this particular area, I'm going to be objecting to leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I rephrase my question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please tell us where the IKM was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us where the IKM was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Please describe it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: It was in Kitovnice in an a hamlet called Jerkic in a summer house, in a summer cottage.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me when you were on duty, there were the two signalsmen and the duty officer. Did you have separate rooms where you were on duty or was it one and the same room where all the three of you were?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: We were together, the three of them, and then some officers complained they didn't want to share the sleeping premises with the signalsmen so we were moved to a container, the signalsmen were.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that while you were on duty, the signalsmen and the duty officers were in the same room?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That has to be a leading question as was the previous one but I didn't object. There is no reason to be asking leading questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I just like to clarify his previous answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but you have every right to do that but you can't do it by means of direct questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's just about sleeping in container, not about duty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please, yes, Mr. McCloskey? You understand -- I can understand that there is a difficulty but we have to find a way around it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I have a difficulty with this last comment as signalling the signals officer so if we could just ask normal questions, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic, please comply.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I will not ask this question again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, do you remember the operation against Srebrenica and when it was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please give us the month and the year?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me whether you remember if the Zvornik Brigade took part in that operation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you personally participate in that operation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You see, I'm not going to ask you about when you left and what you did there before Srebrenica fell. This is not the subject of your testimony here, but I would like to ask you whether you remember how long you stayed, up to when? First of all, can you please tell me what unit you were attached to when you participated in the action against Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: I was the brigade signalsman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you assigned to a particular unit within that brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: The Grbovac company, which was one signalsman short.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I will go back to my previous question now. Can you please tell me up to when you and the Grbovac company you were in remained in that operation against Srebrenica up to what time you remained there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: I was there all the time. I was with the Grbovac company all the time until the moment we left to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember when it was when you left for Zepa?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: We left Srebrenica after the operation, and we went to Crna Rijeka. We spent the night there in a meadow across the road from the barracks, and on the following day, we went to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain something? When you say that you left Srebrenica after the operation, what do you mean by that? What does the word "after the operation" imply? Was that when the army of Republika Srpska entered Srebrenica or did some time lapse or if it did, how much time lapsed from that moment until the moment you left for Crna Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes. When we took Srebrenica, when we entered the town, we left maybe two or three hours later, we went to a river, we took a swim there, then we got on the buses and went in the direction of Crna Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you well? Was it on the same day when the army of Republika Srpska entered Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How much time did it take you to get to Crna Rijeka? Did you arrive there on the same day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember where you spent that night?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Across the road from the barracks in Crna Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I see that you've already answered that. And after that, after that night, where did you go and when did you leave?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Early in the morning, the following morning, we went in the direction of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please tell me, where did you spend the following night? How far did you reach before you had to pack in for the night?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: As soon as we arrived in the territory, fighting started. We pushed them to a certain point by the evening, that's where we stopped, the fighting stopped, and this is where we spent that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And what happened on the following morning? Did you remain there? Did you keep on moving? Did you do something else?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: My company received an order to withdraw towards the buses together with our commander, Macapovic [phoen] because other troops were on their way to replace us and I don't know who these troops were.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And where were you supposed to go once you got on the buses?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: We returned to the brigade in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What was the time of day when you arrived in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Before the noon on that day, but I can't remember exactly when. Maybe around 9.00 or 10.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What happened when you arrived in Zvornik? Did you have some duties to tend to? If so, what kind of duties were those?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: I immediately went to the signals office. My colleague was there. He met me there. And one of the commanders, whose name I can't remember, I don't know whether it was Chief Petrovic or Commander Radic, that person told me to go and report to the IKM.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you that you were supposed to report there immediately or sometime during that day or maybe the following day even?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: He told me to report to the IKM. I did not see him after that. I met Major Obrenovic, whom I called Obren, and I asked him, "Obren, can I have two hours to go home and take a bath and to change my clothes and then report to the IKM?" He said yes. And this is exactly what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, can you tell me when did you finally go to the IKM and where from? In other words, did you go home first and did you go to the IKM from there or from some other place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: I went from my house on foot from -- across Grbovac via Kitovnice on foot to the IKM, on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you give us an estimate of the time from the moment you were given approval to go home to the moment when you arrived at the IKM? Could you give us that estimate or maybe can you give us roughly the time when you arrived at the IKM? When was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: I was there sometime around noon, up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived at the IKM, did you find somebody there? Was somebody there already?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: The duty security officer, Drago Nikolic, was there and a signalsman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know the name of that signalsman who was there at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: No. That signalsman had been borrowed from one of the battalions. To be more precise, it was the Birac Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay at the IKM on that particular occasion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Until 8.00 in the morning on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You have told us that signalsmen shifts normally lasted four days. Can you explain how come you only stayed for one day, from the noon of the previous day to 8.00 the following morning? How do you account for that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Because I had been in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether, on that day, while you were there at the IKM, were there any particular developments, fighting or something of the sort, some special events that would have merited your attention?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have some calls besides the normal ones from the brigade? Did somebody call you from the corps or some other units outside the Zvornik Brigade or some others? Did some high-ranking officers from some other units call you? Do you remember any such thing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Of course I can remember, but we did not have any such calls.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know Lieutenant Colonel Vujadin Popovic at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: I'd heard of him but I did not meet him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if he called you during that night or anybody who introduced themselves as Lieutenant Colonel Vujadin Popovic or something of the sort?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: If they had introduced themselves, I would have known, but since there were people who wanted to be put through to Drago Nikolic directly, which meant that those people knew that he was at the IKM, so I did not ask them to introduce themselves, I would just put them through to Drago Nikolic because that was part of my duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did anybody want to be put through to Drago Nikolic, introducing themselves to you as Vujadin Popovic during that night, or during that day while you were on duty?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, during the day while you were on duty at the IKM, did you share the room with Drago Nikolic, the duty officer at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether during that night, or during that whole day, somebody visited the IKM, an officer, either from your brigade or from other unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Nobody came.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether Drago Nikolic left the IKM at any time during that day or night, or, rather, while on duty on that night?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: He only left when he went to tour the LPN [as interpreted]. That's for 15 or 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what time of day it was when that happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Between 1600 and 1700 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that a regular duty of the officer on duty at the IKM, or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: So that's a regular duty, did I understand you correctly? Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, if you could clarify what an LPN is?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you explain to us what LPA is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Light anti-aircraft artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: So when you say he visited this LPA, was it a unit of the light anti-aircraft artillery or what?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it close to the forward command post or at what distance roughly was it from the IKM, this unit which the officers on duty, doing their regular rounds, had to visit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Well, they were at about 30 metres from us, and the one section, and the three-barrel section was a little further.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said 200 metres, did you? Because the record doesn't reflect that. Did you say that they were 200 metres away, these three -- the men manning the three barrels?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me when you left the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: On the 14th, in the morning, with Mr. Nikolic, to the barracks, at around 8.00, 8.30 at the latest.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And just one more thing that I want to ask you. How did you leave the IKM? What vehicle?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: With a car.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you something else. We have received information -- or rather let me ask you this, first. Do you know who Major Galic is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes, a neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In July 1995, was he -- did he occupy a post in the brigade? Did you know an officer at that time with that same surname of Galic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Mihajlo Galic worked in the personnel department.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: During the time you were on duty, that day and the night that we are discussing, did he come by to the IKM to replace Drago Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And did he appear at the forward command post at all that day or that night?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you stand duty at all with him ever at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just going to ask you another couple of questions. When you arrived after your time on duty at the IKM, and went back to the barracks in the Zvornik Brigade, were you given any new assignments or tasks?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: That day, I was free until 2200 hours, and from 2200 hours I took up the third shift on the switchboard.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: So that was in the brigade itself, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: After that third shift, were you free? Did have you free time or did you have extra duties?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: I had three free days.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: From the time of your arrival in the brigade, that is to say from the time you returned from the IKM, and up until the time you took your three days' leave, did you have any information about any prisoners at all, from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you happen to see any prisoners or any buses passing by the barracks at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: One more thing I'd like to clarify. When you returned from the IKM, you were free until you took up your evening shift, right? How did you spend that interim time? Did you have a rest? Did you have a sleep? Or what?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Well, I slept for a bit and then we played cards for a bit, watched television until the time for my shift came.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did anybody call you, for example, and tell you to go and stand guard over some prisoners, in this interim, this free time you had before you went to take up your duty and shift at the switchboard?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Stojkic. [In English] No further questions, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Zivanovic. We'll have the break now and we'll see what the position is after that. Thank you. 25 minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the examination-in-chief is finished. Mr. Ostojic, you had asked for 15 minutes cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, thank you. And we have no questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Nikolic or Mr. Bourgon, I don't know who is -- you had asked for one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, we do have some questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, please. And would you kindly introduce yourself to him?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Will do, Mr. President and good news is we should be shorter than expected with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what I expected too. Thank you. In the meantime, before you start so that we try and organise ourselves, the -- Mr. Lazarevic, will you be cross-examining this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, no, Your Honour, we are not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no questions for this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which means you will soon be cross-examining, Mr. McCloskey. You had asked for two hours. How long do you anticipate?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Less than an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Less than an hour. All right. So the next witness needs to stay here. And we'll start with him when this one finishes. Mr. Bourgon, sorry for the interruption. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Stojkic. My name is Stephane Bourgon. We have had the pleasure of meeting last Friday but for the sake -- for the record, I'd like to introduce myself formally as counsel representing Drago Nikolic in these proceedings. Firstly, let me begin by confirming with you that there are no other Dragan Stojkic who was working within the communications section of the Zvornik Brigade in 1995. Would that be a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat what he said?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Stojkic, the interpreters had difficulty following your statement. Could you repeat it, please? Could you repeat your reply?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were three more Stojkics in the communication section.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojkic, in terms of those working at the forward command post, was there anybody else called Dragan Stojkic who was working at the forward command post of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojkic, you mentioned a little earlier that you knew who Major Galic was. I take it, then, that Major Galic also knows you personally because you were neighbours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I move on directly to the 14th of July 1995. You mentioned at page 25, lines 24 to 25, that after spending your shift at the forward command post, you left the IKM on the morning of 14 July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So that would mean, then, because it's not part of the record, that you were actually sent to the IKM on the 13th of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. And you mentioned earlier also that one of two persons may have sent you there, either Dragisa Radic or Milisa Petrovic. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So if you were sent on to the forward command post on the 13th of July, this means that you were actually pulled from the Zepa area during the night of 13 July?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That would be inconsistent with his testimony. It's -- also at this point, Mr. President, these are leading questions. And in this particular situation that we find ourselves in, it would be best to have a short discussion outside the presence of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think, in fact I was going to suggest precisely that in particular, particularly in relation to one of the submissions. Does he understand English? Do you understand English, Mr. Stojkic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you want him out of the courtroom or just remove --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It shouldn't take long, just removing is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Just remove the headphones, please. Yes, Mr. McCloskey has raised two matters. One is the -- whether this is leading question or not. And, secondly, whether you have misrepresented in a good sense the witness's previous statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I fail to see any problem here. I am conducting cross-examination. I can put leading questions to the witness and I can suggest to him what I want. I fail to see any problem here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey? He is cross-examining the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, but he can't misstate the facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. But does that mean that the issue of leading question does no longer arise?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If I could alert to you the issue as I see it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you finished your statement or shall I --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'm ready to proceed with the witness, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, no. What I mean to say is about the submission because Mr. McCloskey seems to have got more to say. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We see this particular witness, we have a brief statement of this witness from the Popovic team and we see from that that he's basically was going to testify that Drago Nikolic was not at the forward command post. There is really nothing he has to say about Popovic. So of course we wondered is this a Popovic witness truly or is this really a Nikolic witness in sheep's clothing? And we don't see anything in direct that had to do with Popovic particularly. Yes, we understand this is a joint criminal enterprise but what's the effect of this? What's the effect if we don't have a statement from the true party that's calling him as a witness, the Nikolic team, because he's calling him on cross. But worse yet is that we are now seeing leading questions to a friendly witness. In this Tribunal, you have a right to cross-examine witnesses against you. Now, this as you know is one of those issue that's being litigated now. There has been interesting rulings in ICTR on it and I don't really want to get into that now. But the important thing for you, as the Trial Chamber, is do you want to listen to leading questions of a friendly witness? In all of my years in doing this, I have never found judges, nor juries for that matter, that appreciated leading questions of friendly witness because it's basically the lawyer testifying. In fact leading questions on cross-examination is something that I'm over the years trying to convince my civil law colleagues has had some reasonable place in this place. But especially a witness like this, in what has happened before, I don't think leading questions are appropriate in this context. This is a Nikolic witness, should have been a Nikolic witness from the beginning, they've done this interesting strategy. Mr. Bourgon acknowledged that he met with this person on Friday. So what we see is a Nikolic witness. He shouldn't be leading him. I don't think the Court wants -- should want to hear leading questions of this witness. And so I would ask, without having to get into all of this area of the law for you to take it into your discretion to allow Mr. Bourgon to ask questions of this witness but not leading, please, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon? And then Mr. Zivanovic as well because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Judge for the record, Mr. McCloskey, line 4 -- line 5 on previous page should be -- should read "was" instead of "was not." Could you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. It's my understanding that it's -- that Drago Nikolic was at the forward command post, Galic was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment, Mr. Bourgon. Mr. Zivanovic, you've been directly involved in this debate. Do you wish to comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would just like to remind Mr. McCloskey that we challenged the testimony of the witness PW-168 and it is his allegation that Mr. Nikolic had a phone call at -- sorry, at the IKM and it is the reason because I took this witness as my witness. It is not any strategy or anything else but just it was just this reason, and I -- we had a -- we have an interest to challenge as well the testimony of the witness Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Once again I fail so see any difficulties with what my colleague is saying other than the fact that I really don't appreciate his suggestions that we are entering into some kind of strategy business with witnesses, because we are not. We -- this is Mr. Zoran Zivanovic's witness and now I'm conducting cross-examination. If the Court feels that my questions are too much leading, I will suffer the consequences myself when the weight will be assessed by the Judges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. And that's exactly the position that we take. You've just summarised it in one short sentence. So, please proceed with your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Wait. All right. He's got the headphones on now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojkic, we will continue with this cross-examination. The question I was asking of you is that you mentioned in response to a question, on page 25, lines 24 to 25, that you left the forward command post, the IKM, the morning of the 14th of July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So you were sent to the IKM the morning of the 13th July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And can we understand from this that you were immediately prior, the night prior, that's when you were pulled out from Zepa, along with your company, and I believe you mentioned the Grbovac company; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: On the 13th, in the morning, we were pulled out.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, the question I have for you, Mr. Stojkic, is that other witnesses have testified in this case to the fact that the Zvornik Brigade component that was sent to Zepa was actually pulled back on the 15 of July, so I'd like to know if you can explain how you can be so sure that you were pulled out on the 13th of July along with your company.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: I'm sure because I went with my company commander, and as for the rest of the brigade, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I move on then to the 13th of July when you actually were sent to the IKM and I refer you to page 24, lines 17 to 18. Now, don't be scared about those pages. This is just to alert my colleague to where I'm referring him to one of your previous responses. So on the 13th of July you mentioned that you were at the Standard barracks between 9.00 and 10.00 in the morning, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Did you actually see Major Obrenovic at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Can you explain to us Mr. Stojkic, how is it that you can call Major Obrenovic who was chief of staff of the Zvornik Brigade, how come you called him Obren, as you say?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Because we were really on very good terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And on that day it is Major Obrenovic who allowed you to go home to take a bath for a couple of hours upon your request, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you also mentioned earlier that you went to your house which is in Celopek and that you walked to the IKM by foot. What's the distance approximately between your house and Celopek in the IKM?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Across the hill, across Grbovac maybe 12 kilometers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So you walked all that distance by foot to go to the IKM?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: You mentioned that when arrived at the IKM - correct me if I'm wrong - there appears to have been two persons present there. One was Drago Nikolic, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Ane the other person was a communicator and it appears you don't remember the name but you mention Birac battalion. Can you tell us anything else about this second person?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: I only know that he had been borrowed from a battalion to assist temporarily because there were not enough of our brigade signalsmen. We had been in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now if I tried to locate this man, can you give us any information about him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: On page 21, lines 10 to 11, you mentioned that there was some kind of a container where communicators would sleep at times. My question is: Was that container in use on 13 July and did you sleep there that night?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: That night we did not sleep in the container because Mr. Nikolic never objected to another person, i.e., a signalsman, sharing the same room with him for the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: You mentioned on page 27, lines 15 to 16, that Drago Nikolic left to the LPN, and you explained that to us, that this was the air defence artillery or something like that. Or LPA or LPN? What would that be?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: LPA.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: LPA. Thank you. Now, are you familiar with the fact that close to the IKM there was some kind of an observation trench? Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And did Drago Nikolic go to that observation trench during that day, to your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: I know only about the LPA. A trench was near that, so it is possible that he went to the trench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Let's proceed. It seems to be working fine now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for your patience.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojkic, we will continue with my questions. Can you confirm that during the period you were at the forward command post, from the 13th of July until the 14th in the morning, that Drago Nikolic did not leave the IKM? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Is there any possibility, for instance, that you were sleeping and Drago Nikolic could have left the IKM without you knowing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: That night I did not sleep at all because I was on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojkic, do you know a family by the name Jerkic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Can you tell us who this family is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: That's the family which gave -- which was next to our IKM. Actually their house was next to the house where our IKM was so we would see them every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Was there any special relationship that developed between this family and the people working at the IKM?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: No, but we were really very, very good friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: When we met on Friday, you told me that this -- that Milka Jerkic and her son would bring you cheese, coffee and other goods. Is that what you mean by saying that you were good friends?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was it, by and large.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Do you recall if anyone from that family came to the IKM on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Yes. The young Mica, Milka's son, came.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And what was the purpose of his visit, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: He was a young lad and he would always hang out with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, you already responded to this question earlier but can you confirm that during that period you were at the IKM from the 13th to the 14th, there were no other visitors there during that time frame; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: That's correct, nobody came.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And just to end this topic about the Jerkic family, is it possible that a duty officer working at the IKM would not know who the Jerkic family is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, on page 26 at lines 20 to 24, you mentioned that those who would call would know that Drago Nikolic was on duty and that they would ask for him. My question is: Did these people identify themselves when they would call?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: They would only introduce themselves if they knew who the duty officer at the IKM was.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter may not have gotten the answer correctly. Could the witness please repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer, Mr. Stojkic? The interpreter might not have understood all of it. Maybe you could get closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you have identified the problem. Madam Usher has already asked him to move nearer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please repeat the question, then?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Yes. The question is, if I go back to the exact question which was a little earlier on that page, did the people who called at the forward command post identify themselves when they called?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: According to the rules, they should have introduced themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And to your memory, did Drago Nikolic have a conversation that day with the Chief of Staff of the Zvornik Brigade, Major Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: I can't answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And if -- or let me say that in a different way. When Drago Nikolic was on the phone at the IKM, would you hear the content of any conversations he would have?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: The contents?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Did you hear him? Did you hear the conversations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: The duty officers, when they were on the phone, normally asked -- the signalsman would leave and step out on to the terrace.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Would that be for every conversation or...

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Well, we simply did not want to disturb them while they were talking.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And just to -- if there was a conversation between Drago Nikolic and another officer, or Major Obrenovic, talking about the arrival of prisoners and the killing of prisoners, would you remember that kind of conversation, if you had heard it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Of course I would remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And do you remember hearing any such conversations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And do you remember ever leaving outside on the terrace while Drago Nikolic was having any conversations that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: I don't know how many times he actually used the telephone while on duty. Maybe once or twice perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And did you go outside for these conversations or did you stay inside? To the best of your memory.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: I stayed in. We were playing cards. And the cards were on the table. His conversations were really short and as soon as he put down the telephone, we continued playing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: When you left the IKM on the 14th in the morning, what happened to the other communicator, the man from the Birac Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: He stayed on, but somebody else came to help him later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And do you know who came later on to replace you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Of the four of us who were regularly there at the IKM, I'm not sure but it could have been only Zoran Acimovic, Dragisa Savic or Jovo Bogdanovic, one of the three.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And do you know who replaced Drago Nikolic on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: One of his colleagues from the security, I believe. But I'm not sure whether it was Trbic maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: When you arrive at the barracks on that day, on the 14th of July, you responded earlier that you played cards until you took up that night shift and you mentioned the third night shift. What time did you actually begin the night shift at the Zvornik Brigade that evening?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: We did not play cards all the time. I took a little nap, and my shift started at 22 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And what actually did you do during that shift? What were your responsibilities at Standard? What kind of shift was that and what did you do?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: It was just like any other shift when you work at switchboard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: What's your duties? What do you do at the switchboard?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJKIC
utterances.text: Well, whatever calls you receive, and there are persons asking for an officer, you would put them through. That's what we did. Just connecting people.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'd like to show you now, Mr. Stojkic, an exhibit. That is P347. And we referred to that exhibit before. That is the duty officer logbook at the IKM. If I can ask my colleague to maybe give the original to the witness, we have made arrangements for that. That's P347. And if I can have on the -- on e-court, the English page 6 of that book. Do you have the -- yes. If you can give the witness the book and if you can open the book on page, in the original should be page 8 and where there is an entry for 13th of July 1995.
